Reveal state renders title 'MỞ SECRET BOX THÀNH CÔNG' with the awarded badge image at intrinsic 64x64, not upscaled. — verified: ran S09 GREEN locally; secret-box-badge-asset.ts renders at SECRET_BOX_BADGE_ASSET_SIZE=64 with no upscale, badge boundingBox asserted <=65px in S07.

When unopened count reaches 0 inside the open modal, the instruction line is hidden and the box is no longer clickable. — verified: ran S10 GREEN locally, instruction hidden and box disabled after draining to 0.

The dialog closes via its X button and via Escape, following the repo's native <dialog> pattern. — verified: ran S11/S12 GREEN locally; use-secret-box-dialog.ts mirrors use-kudos-compose-dialog.ts's ref-callback + onCancel pattern.

Badge draw and unopened count are computed server-side; client-side tampering with the count or badge id cannot change what is persisted. — verified: open_secret_box() is SECURITY DEFINER, resolves auth.uid() itself with no user-id parameter; SecretBoxLauncher never decrements 'live' locally, only from result.unopened; parseOpeningRow in secret-box.ts fails closed (throws) on any malformed/unrecognized RPC response shape, exercised by secret-box.test.ts.

Two concurrent/double-clicked open requests never consume more boxes than the viewer is entitled to. — verified by reading open_secret_box(): pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(v_user_id::text,0)) serializes per-user calls, entitlement/opened are re-SELECTed AFTER lock acquisition inside the same transaction as the INSERT, so a blocked second call re-reads post-commit state and correctly raises no_boxes_left when exhausted.

Entitlement equals floor(sum(kudos.heart_count where sender_id = viewer)/5) minus count of that viewer's openings. — verified in both the RPC SQL and src/dal/kudos-stats.ts's getKudosStats (used for initial render) — both read kudos.sender_id, never receiver_id, matching the sender-credits-hearts rule.

findings.summary: Catch-all in openSecretBoxAction swallows every unrecognized error (thrown Postgres error, createClient() failure) into {ok:false, reason:'unknown'} with no server-side logging, making an unexpected failure mode invisible in production even though the client-facing behavior (no leaked stack trace) is correct.
